articles.title: Leonid memories
articles.summary: This article provides vivid personal accounts of observing intense Leonid meteor showers in 2001 and 2002. Observers recount seeing thousands of meteors, including spectacular fireballs with long-lasting trains, from locations like Alice Springs and the North Atlantic. The narrations emphasize the high rates and memorable nature of these events, with detailed counts and descriptions of peak activity.

articles.title: Saturn gets crabby
articles.summary: This article details celestial events occurring in early January 2003, with a primary focus on Saturn's transit across the dim Crab Nebula (M1) on January 4-5. It also covers Earth's perihelion, a recent spectacular sighting of the aurora borealis accompanied by meteors, and observational tips for Jupiter, Venus, and Mars. The author encourages readers to observe these phenomena and offers insights into what to look for.

articles.title: Shallow Sky Observations
articles.summary: This article offers a monthly guide for amateur astronomers, detailing planetary positions and events like Venus passing Pluto and Mercury's inferior conjunction. It provides advice for new telescope owners, emphasizing lunar observation with key features to learn and highlighting the unforgettable first views of the Moon, Saturn, Jupiter, and M42. Additionally, it includes a 'Starhop' guide to specific deep-sky objects, such as open clusters and a planetary nebula in constellations like Camelopardalis, complete with personal observing notes.

articles.title: A New Look At The Moon
articles.summary: This article encourages amateur astronomers, particularly those new to telescopes, to observe the Moon, highlighting it as an ideal target due to its high contrast, abundant detail, and suitability for all telescope types. It offers practical advice for optimal viewing, such as observing the terminator, using higher magnifications, and notes that the first half of the year is best for high-altitude lunar viewing. The author also debunks the necessity of moon filters for beginners and recommends specific resources for lunar mapping.

articles.title: School star parties
articles.summary: Bob Havner emphasizes the San Jose Astronomical Association's commitment to public outreach through school star parties, noting their importance in introducing astronomy to young people and their parents. Despite successful events and increasing membership, there's a significant need for more member volunteers at school events, which often host large groups. Havner encourages members to participate, highlighting the rewarding experience and providing a January 2003 schedule, contact information, and resources for new volunteers.

articles.title: "Take me to the river..."
articles.summary: This article serves as an observing guide, leading amateur astronomers through various deep-sky objects primarily visible in the winter sky. It provides detailed star-hopping instructions, visual descriptions, and personal observing notes for several open clusters (including Kemble's Cascade, NGC 1528, M45, and NGC 1647) and the planetary nebula NGC 1535, spanning constellations like Perseus, Taurus, and Eridanus. The guide encourages observers to use binoculars, finders, and telescopes to explore these celestial targets.

articles.title: Telescope Making
articles.summary: Mike Koop is leading a "Telescope Making" class beginning Saturday, January 11, at 7:30 p.m. at Houge Park. The class, which is easier and more fun than expected, will cover mirror making and scope building, utilizing a Foucault tester, and will meet bi-monthly throughout the first half of 2003. Attendees can work on personal projects, contribute to a "Community Mirror," and learn about all aspects of amateur telescope making.

articles.title: January speaker Dr. Nick Kanas
articles.summary: Dr. Nick Kanas, a Professor of Psychiatry and long-time amateur astronomer, is announced as the January speaker. His presentation, titled "Of epicycles and unicorns: celestial mapping in the golden age," will explore pictorial celestial cartography from the 1600s to 1800s. Kanas, who also researches psychosocial factors in astronauts, will share insights from his extensive study and collection of antiquarian star atlases.

articles.title: SJAA Loaner Scope Status
articles.summary: The SJAA Loaner Scope program provides telescopes to members, outlining their current availability status. The article lists scopes that are immediately available, those currently on loan with due dates, and those with extended loan periods, along with a waiting list for popular items. Members can contact Mike Koop to borrow a scope or be placed on a waiting list.
